alex.s: heads-up — saw steady memory growth on long-context perf run (LLama-70B-mqa + Mistral-7B variants). KV residency keeps climbing past expected plateau, looks like eviction isn’t compacting pages fast enough. anyone seen this pattern recently?
maria_r: which model and config? seq len, batching, kernel? :thinking:
tylerg: run details: single-client stress, seq_growth 64->4k over ~20min, batching disabled, continuous prefix caching ON, kernel autotuner chose mixed small/large at ~2k tokens.
alex.s: exact run id: perf-4832, infra-bot uploaded artifacts. profiler shows gradual increase in "resident_kv_pages" even when evictions reported. suspect fragmentation + sweep policy timing mismatch with rope scaling.
infra-bot: perf-runner: job 4832 completed — artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood/internal/perf/4832/prof.tar.gz :white_check_mark:
jun: can you paste the short profiler summary?
alex.s: sure — truncated metrics from perf agent:
```
model=Llama-70B-mqa  seq=4096
wall=1260s  tokens=2.4M
page_allocs=14230  evicted_pages=6180  compactions=12
resident_kv_pages=8050 -> 11800 (end)
avg_page_fill=0.43  fragmentation_ratio=0.36
swap_count=0  eviction_cycles=27
```
maria_r: compactions=12 seems low for that many evictions. maybe compaction is gated by age or free-window threshold. rope scaling may be changing token growth pattern so pages never hit the compaction trigger.
ops_lead: note that GQA vs MQA change how KV frames align: MQA interleaves smaller frames per layer which can increase fragmentation under our current slab allocator. that matches the Llama-MQA data.
tylerg: also saw kernel switching at 2048 tokens, kernel switch does a quick re-layout of KV pointers — if compaction runs concurrently it may miss coalescing opportunities.
alex.s: hypothesis: eviction marks pages free but sweep_policy has both an "age_threshold_s" and a "min_free_pages" gate; under long-growing contexts with rope scaling the free pages are small scattered holes so "min_free_pages" never reached and fragmentation climbs.
maria_r: can we reproduce with a small test: force sequential token growth and a synthetic prompt to produce fragmentation, then toggle sweep params?
jun: yes, I can run a variant — adding a debug flag `--force-sweep-after-evict` is quick. also will dump page-residency histogram per layer.
infra-bot: job 4833 queued (debug-sweep). ETA ~12m.
alex.s: if that reproduces, next steps: 1) add per-model compaction heuristics (lower min_free_pages for MQA), 2) try an alternative eviction policy that prefers contiguous slab ranges, 3) add metric alert when fragmentation_ratio > 0.25 for > 5min.
maria_r: also evaluate batching heuristics — dynamic batchingmight merge small requests into larger contiguous KV writes reducing holes. test with `batch_merge_threshold=0.2`.
tylerg: quick note: kernel selection logic currently optimizes for compute latency but ignores downstream compaction cost. we should feed compaction penalty into kernel scoring.
ops_lead: agreed. ops: can we get a medium-priority ticket for a two-week spike to instrument and try policy changes? assign to runtime/infra pair. :eyes:
alex.s: I'll open the repro PR and a draft RFC for sweep policy tweaks. pinging @maria_r @tylerg for review.
maria_r: ack, will review tests + histograms.
jun: perf-run 4833 finished — reproduces fragmentation rise. attaching small log snippet: 
```
job=4833 model=Mistral-7B seq=4096
page_allocs=9800  evicted_pages=4200  compactions=3
resident_kv_pages=5200 -> 7700
fragmentation_ratio=0.41
```
alex.s: perfect repro. opening ticket with logs and request for a telemetry flag to be enabled in staging. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
